title: security(k6): stop persisting Supabase auth tokens into k6 summary artifacts
summary: Closes the recurring secret-exposure mechanism behind #643: k6 load-test summary handlers serialized the full run data object (including setup_data, which caches the Supabase auth token) into committed artifacts/benchmarks/ JSON, writing a live role=authenticated JWT at raw_data.setup_data.authToken on every run. A new runtime-agnostic redaction module (tools/scripts/k6/lib/redact.js, 13 Vitest cases) now sanitizes every summary before write — dropping setup_data and deep-redacting secret-keyed values and JWT-shaped strings — across authenticated-, comprehensive-, quick- and load-test scripts. Adds persistent-token acquisition (K6_AUTH_TOKEN env, reused across runs to avoid Supabase auth rate-limit flakiness) via an env-first setup() path and a stdout-only get-auth-token.mjs helper; the token is never written to a committed file (.env.k6.local is gitignored, .env.example carries the empty shape). The 18 expired historical fingerprints in .gitleaksignore are retained (they pin immutable history for the nightly full-history scan; dropping them would red it with no history rewrite) and the follow-up note records the source is now fixed.

gate_results.detail: sanitizeSummaryData(data) wired into every summary-writing handler (authenticated-load-test.js, comprehensive-load-test.js, quick-test.js, load-test.js). Drops setup_data + deep-redacts secret keys and JWT strings.
Unit test asserts JSON.stringify(sanitizeSummaryData(realisticSummaryWithSetupData)) contains no 'eyJ' and no 'setup_data' while retaining metrics (p(95)).

tools/scripts/k6/lib/redact.test.ts — 13 cases: secret-key masking (all spellings), nested/array JWT redaction, setup_data stripping, non-object input, input immutability. Module has zero k6 imports (Vitest-runnable).

resolveAuthToken() returns __ENV.K6_AUTH_TOKEN when set (logs 'no re-auth'), else the live Supabase grant. setup() in all three authenticating scripts uses it. get-auth-token.mjs acquires once, prints to stdout only.

No JWT/token literal in the diff: test JWTs are base64url-built at runtime; helper never writes a committed path; .env.example K6_AUTH_TOKEN is empty; .env.k6.local ignored via .env*.local. gitleaks + trivy green on the PR.
The 18 historical k6 JWT fingerprints stay in .gitleaksignore (immutable history, nightly full-history scan, no rewrite, all expired). Follow-up note updated to record the source is fixed.
ESLint clean on all changed JS/TS + the .mjs helper; redact.test.ts green (13/13); full pre-ship run at the final SHA (see notes).
Isolated worktree, Node 22, local test DB intelliflow_test :5433. No prod Supabase, no key rotation, no destructive migration.

notes: SEC-643 is a security follow-up to #637 (found during ENG-OPS-003.Gap5-AuditsUnblock) and is tracked attestation-only, like the other ENG-OPS-003 gaps — no Sprint_plan.csv row, so csv_mutations is empty. Issue fix option 1 (redact at source) is implemented; option 3 (drop fingerprints) is deliberately NOT taken because the fingerprints pin immutable historical commits and dropping them would red the nightly full-history scan without a forbidden history rewrite — the tokens are all expired so this is safe. spec.md/plan.md live beside this file but are gitignored (.specify spec/plan pattern); this attestation is the committed record.
